text: The word of the LORD that came to Hosea son of Beeri in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel.

When the LORD first spoke through Hosea, the LORD said to him: "Go, take for yourself a wife of prostitution and children of prostitution, for the land commits great prostitution by turning away from the LORD."

versions.text: When the LORD first spoke through Hosea, the LORD said to him: "Go, take for yourself a wife of prostitution and children of prostitution, for the land is guilty of flagrant prostitution in turning away from the LORD."
versions.explanation: The infinitive-absolute construction זָנֹה תִזְנֶה is verbal ('the land commits great whoredom'), not adjectival ('is guilty of'). Also, 'in turning away' is awkward for oral reading; 'by turning away' flows better and matches מֵאַחֲרֵי (from following after).

text: So he went and took Gomer daughter of Diblaim, and she conceived and bore him a son.
And the LORD said to him, "Name him Jezreel, for in a little while I will punish the house of Jehu for the blood shed at Jezreel, and I will put an end to the kingdom of the house of Israel.
On that day I will break Israel's bow in the Valley of Jezreel."

She conceived again and bore a daughter. And the LORD said to him, "Name her No Mercy, for I will no longer show mercy to the house of Israel; I will certainly not forgive them.[^1]

[^1]: Or "that I should in any way forgive them"; the Hebrew clause is difficult and has also been understood as "I will utterly take them away."

versions.text: She conceived again and bore a daughter. And the LORD said to him, "Name her No Mercy, for I will no longer show mercy to the house of Israel; I will certainly not forgive them.
versions.explanation: The symbolic name is translated but the Hebrew form is lost. A brief footnote giving the Hebrew name preserves the link to the wordplay in later chapters (see Hosea 2:1, 23) without burdening the reading text.

versions.text:
She conceived again and bore a daughter. And the LORD said to him, "Name her No Mercy,[^1] for I will no longer show mercy to the house of Israel; I will certainly not forgive them.

[^1]: Hebrew Lo-Ruhamah, meaning "she has not received mercy."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew נָשֹׂא אֶשָּׂא לָהֶם contains no negative particle; the negation is carried over from the preceding clause. Since this is a recognized crux, a footnote noting the alternative readings would guard against overstating the certainty of the rendering.

text: But I will show mercy to the house of Judah, and I will save them by the LORD their God. I will not save them by bow or sword or battle, by horses or horsemen."
After she had weaned No Mercy, she conceived and bore a son.

And the LORD said, "Name him Not My People,[^1] for you are not my people, and I will not be your God.[^2]

[^1]: Hebrew Lo-Ammi.

[^2]: Hebrew "and I will not be yours"; the wording echoes the divine name revealed in Exodus 3:14.

versions.text: And the LORD said, "Name him Not My People, for you are not my people, and I will not be your God."
versions.explanation: 'God' is supplied (the Hebrew reads simply 'and I will not be yours'), and the verb אֶהְיֶה deliberately echoes the divine self-designation. Footnotes giving the Hebrew name and the literal wording add value without disturbing the flow of the reading text.
